Theme

cigarette noun

also cigarettes, cigar, smoke a cigarette, smoking, no smoking, tobacco, pack of cigarettes, smoker, smoke (a cigarette)

modern

Traupman 291
M-O s.v. cigarette

sigarellum, sigarellī n.

noun, second declension

a cigarette

The modern word, a diminutive of sigārum, cigar. A packet of cigarettes is capsella sigarellōrum (Traupman 291).

Other words

  • bacillum tabācī — a cigarette (a little stick of tobacco)

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. cigarette

    A description on classical bacillum, a little stick; tobacco is tabācum (Morgan–Owens, after Linnaeus).

  • 1sigārum: long a (Traupman sigarum, unmarked). Morgan–Owens s.v. cigar writes sigârum. With the long vowel the Latin stress falls where Spanish cigarro, the source of the word, has it, as the house does for modern names with no Latin quantity (Lisbōna).

    sigārum1, sigārī n. — a cigar

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 291; M-O s.v. cigar

  • fūmum sigarellī sūgere — to smoke a cigarette

    also used · modern · Traupman 291, 381; M-O s.v. smoke vb. (cigarettes, etc.): fūmum (alicujus reī) haurīre

    Traupman’s phrase; Morgan–Owens gives fūmum haurīre from eighteenth- and nineteenth-century writers, and Egger’s no-smoking sign, ubi fūmus haurīrī vetātur.

  • fistula nicotiāna — a cigarette (as some modern Latinists use it)

    avoid · modern · M-O s.v. cigarette

    Morgan–Owens warns that fistula, a tube, fits a pipe, not a cigarette, and was so used of pipes in earlier centuries.

Examples

  • Hīc fūmum haurīre nōn licet.

    No smoking here.composed

  • capsella sigarellōrum
